clue.text: Plonk is knocked back in warehouse

indicators.note: the reversed little word sits in the middle of the storage place

parts.note: a depot is a storage warehouse

indicators.note: knocked back means the word is is turned round, read backwards

explanation.surface: A drinker downs cheap wine (plonk) at a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plonk' and 'knocked back' suggest cheap wine being drunk; plonk is in fact the verb, to put down heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To plonk something is to set it down heavily, a casual synonym of placing or depositing it.

clue.text: Criminal Investigation Department filling most of legal document for judge

indicators.note: filling means the initials go inside the shortened document
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
CID is the abbreviation for the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives' paperwork fills most of a legal document for a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Judge is the verb here: to make a ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide is to settle a matter, to rule or arbitrate on it.

clue.text: Priest initially up for worship

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of Priest

parts.note: to up a price is to raise it

explanation.surface: A priest is first up to lead the worship.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise God is to glorify and adore, a form of worship.

clue.text: Rubbish our dustmen cleared

indicators.note: rubbish indicates the letters are a mess to be sorted

explanation.surface: The refuse collectors cleared away our rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To surmount an obstacle is to get over it, as a jumper clears a fence.

clue.text: Recurrent idea from article supported by this writer

parts.note: the is the definite article
this writer means the setter, me

explanation.surface: A writer keeps returning to an idea in an article he supports.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a motif, a subject that runs through a work.

clue.text: Intolerable sentimentality from European after claret's drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the wine's letters are befuddled and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of claret, the 's acting as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone becomes unbearably soppy after drinking claret.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle figuratively means cloying, excessive sentiment, from the sticky syrup.

clue.text: Voyager's tense tangle with the French Resistance

definitions.note: the 's is 'is' joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
to ravel is to tangle
le is French for the
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A traveller tangles with the French Resistance in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyager is someone on a journey, one who travels.

clue.text: Truss upset about No 10 departure

indicators.note: about means the reversed word surrounds the numeral
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to truss is to tie
X is the Roman numeral for 10

explanation.surface: Liz Truss's brief stay ending in a departure from Number 10 Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Truss and No 10 call up the Prime Minister and Downing Street, but truss is just the verb, to tie.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a way out, a leaving.

clue.text: Bubbly people in tents keeping hot

indicators.note: keeping means holding the letter inside

parts.note: campers sleep in tents
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: Campers keep cool in hot weather with fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is British slang for champagne, the sparkling wine also called bubbly.

clue.text: Uniform relative put on good for church service

parts.note: uniform means even
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative in uniform turns up for a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service.

clue.text: One might sit on this cold rug

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
rug is slang for hair, especially a toupee

explanation.surface: A cold rug sounds like something you'd perch on.
explanation.walkthrough: Rug looks like a floor covering, but it is slang for a head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a seat, furniture designed for a person to sit on.

clue.text: I created a new Scotch

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of inventing a new whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch looks like whisky, but here it is the verb meaning to put an end to.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to stamp it out completely, to destroy it.

clue.text: Record finished before Edward realised

parts.note: a record is a disc
finished means over
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward realised that a record had ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to find it out, to come to know it.

clue.text: Work in shop usually

indicators.note: in says the answer is contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A remark that work usually happens in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is Latin for a work, used especially of musical compositions.

clue.text: Hostile Finn rudely waving

indicators.note: waving means the letters are moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Finn waving rudely in a hostile way.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfriendly means antagonistic, not well-disposed.

clue.text: Wearing thong, enthralling the Spanish with flash finally

parts.note: wearing something means being in it

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the thong holds the Spanish article inside

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
to flash is to move quickly, to run

explanation.surface: Racy picture of someone in a thong charming a Spaniard and flashing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, when everything has played out over time.

clue.text: Fashionable chap opening no letters to begin with

indicators.note: no letters to begin with means both words lose their first letters

explanation.surface: A trendy fellow opens something, with no letters to start off.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first letter of each word: chap becomes HAP, opening becomes PENING.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening is slang for trendy or lively, where the action is.

clue.text: I come about imprisoning convict being cost-effective

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking the convict inside the shuffled letters
about suggests the letters are moved around

parts.note: a con is a convict

explanation.surface: Someone visits jail to see a convict in an economical way.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic can mean profitable or worth doing financially, giving value for money.

clue.text: Horse-like creatures from Oxford and Cambridge perhaps eating grain

indicators.note: eating means the universities enclose the grain

parts.note: Oxford and Cambridge are examples of universities, unis
corn is grain

explanation.surface: Mythical horses at Oxbridge munching grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Unicorns are mythical animals resembling a horse with a single horn.

clue.text: Caretaker following Conservative peer

parts.note: a caretaker manager or government is a temporary one

explanation.surface: A caretaker succeeds a Tory member of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: Peer looks like a lord; here it is an equal, someone of the same age.
explanation.definitionFit: A contemporary is a person of the same generation, an equal or fellow.

clue.text: John turned up grasping and savage

indicators.note: grasping means holding the word and inside
turned up in a down clue means read backwards

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is lav

explanation.surface: John turns up, grabs things and acts savagely.
explanation.walkthrough: John is not a man here but slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is a destructive barbarian, a wrecker.

clue.text: Only impel odd characters to leave bank

indicators.note: odd characters to leave means the first, third and fifth letters go, keeping the even ones

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: Telling odd people to leave a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely means simply, nothing more than.

clue.text: Pinch jug

explanation.walkthrough: Jug looks like a pitcher to pinch; it is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to steal informally and also, as a noun, a prison or police station in British slang.

clue.text: Careful French composer reduced price

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the composer's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Léo Delibes was a French composer, of Coppélia
a rate is a price charged

explanation.surface: A careful French composer who has cut his price.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate means done with care and intention, unhurried and considered.

clue.text: Perfect international business transaction

parts.note: a deal is a business transaction

explanation.surface: An international deal that's just perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means flawless, exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: Dress is lifted outside topless bar

indicators.note: outside means the reversed word wraps round the shortened bar
lifted in a down clue means raised up, read backwards
topless means the first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A dress is hitched up outside a topless bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is a South Asian garment, a draped length of cloth worn as a dress.

clue.text: Spoil fish at home with last bit of cheese spread

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
a gar is a long-snouted fish
in means at home

indicators.note: last bit of picks the final letter of cheese

explanation.surface: Ruining a fish dish at home with the last of the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute spread on bread.

clue.text: Avoid deer, holding leads of dogs gingerly

indicators.note: holding means the deer surrounds the picked letters

parts.note: a doe is a female deer

indicators.note: leads of means the leading letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Dodging a deer while gingerly holding dogs on their leads.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to evade or sidestep something.

clue.text: Swearing about American rat

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
US means American
to rat or sing is to inform on someone

explanation.surface: Cursing about an American rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: Rat looks like the animal; it is the verb to grass, to sing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Cussing is informal American for using bad language, cursing.

clue.text: Allegiance from kings maybe after change of direction?

indicators.note: change of direction swaps right for left, the letter R becoming L

parts.note: kings are an example of royalty

explanation.surface: Wondering whether kings command allegiance after a policy U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) and L (left) are the directions swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalty is faithful support, fidelity owed to a sovereign or cause.
